  • rewrite the genetic code using a repair template. (1 mark)

  • Ans: They are the most common type of genetic variation and are highly stable. (1 mark)
  • Utility: Excellent for Genome-Wide Association Studies (GWAS) to link genetic variations
  • with complex diseases and drug responses. (1 mark)

questions.question: Why is maintaining sterility especially important during tissue processing? / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Why is maintaining sterility especially important during tissue processing? [U] / [CO1]
  • Ans: Tissues removed from a biological specimen lose their immune system protection and
  • are entirely vulnerable to microscopic contaminants. (1 mark)
  • Since cell culture media is extremely rich in nutrients, any introduced bacteria or fungi will
  • grow exponentially faster than the mammalian cells, outcompeting and killing the valuable
  • primary tissue. (1 mark)
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Name the chemicals used for base-specific cleavage in Maxam–Gilbert sequencing. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Name the chemicals used for base-specific cleavage in Maxam–Gilbert sequencing [K] /
  • [CO3]
  • Ans: Dimethyl sulfate for Guanine (G), Hydrazine for Cytosine and Thymine (C and T).
  • (1 mark)
  • Hydrazine + salt for Cytosine (C only), and Piperidine for the actual cleavage. (1 mark)
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Define Quantitative Fluorescent PCR (QF-PCR). / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Define Quantitative Fluorescent PCR (QF-PCR). [K] / [CO2]
  • Ans: A rapid DNA amplification technique that uses fluorescently labeled primers to amplify
  • Short Tandem Repeats (STRs). (1 mark)
  • It is used for rapid prenatal diagnosis of chromosome abnormalities (e.g., Trisomy 21). (1 mark)
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: State two advantages of NGS over traditional sequencing methods. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• State two advantages of NGS over traditional sequencing methods. [U] / [CO3]
  • Ans: Advantage 1: It is incredibly fast because it can read millions of DNA strands all at the
  • same time, producing huge amounts of data very quickly. (1 mark)
  • Advantage 2: It is much cheaper when sequencing large amounts of DNA, and it is highly
  • accurate at finding very rare genetic mutations. (1 mark)
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Mention various applications of VNTRs in medical genetics. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Mention various applications of VNTRs in medical genetics. [E] / [CO2]
  • Ans: They are highly polymorphic and are used heavily in DNA fingerprinting for forensics
  • and paternity testing. (1 mark)
  • Clinically, they are used for genetic linkage analysis to track how diseases are inherited within
  • families, and to monitor bone marrow engraftment after transplants. (1 mark)
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Describe how transcriptomics helps in understanding disease mechanisms. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Describe how transcriptomics helps in understanding disease mechanisms. [E] / [CO3]
  • Ans: Transcriptomics measures active gene expression levels and identifies differentially
  • expressed genes or alternative splicing events in a cell. (1 mark)
  • This data helps researchers classify cancers, understand host-pathogen interactions, and monitor
  • how cells respond to specific drugs. (1 mark)
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Why is WES focused on exons rather than introns? / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Why is WES focused on exons rather than introns? [E] / [CO3]
  • Ans: Whole Exome Sequencing (WES) specifically targets the protein-coding regions (exons)
  • of the genome. (1 mark)
  • It focuses here because the vast majority (approximately 85%) of known disease-causing
  • mutations occur within these functional coding regions, making it a highly efficient diagnostic
  • tool. (1 mark)
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain the difference between Global and Local sequence alignment. / [CO5]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the difference between Global and Local sequence alignment. [U] / [CO5]
  • Ans: Global Alignment: Attempts to align the entire length of two sequences from end to end,
  • which is best for sequences that are highly similar and of similar length. (1 mark)
  • Local Alignment: Searches for the most similar sub-regions or conserved motifs within two
  • sequences, which is best for comparing sequences that are largely divergent. (1 mark)
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: How does the "Minimum ORF Length" parameter help reduce false positives? / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• How does the "Minimum ORF Length" parameter help reduce false positives?
  • [U] / [CO4]
  • Ans: Random DNA sequences can frequently generate short, non-functional Open Reading Frames
  • (ORFs) purely by chance. (1 mark)
  • Setting a minimum length filter eliminates these tiny, random reading frames, leaving only the
  • sequences that have a statistically significant probability of coding for a real functional protein.
  • (1 mark)
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: What specific information is found in the 'FEATURES' table of a Gen Bank record? / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• What specific information is found in the 'FEATURES' table of a GenBank
  • record? [U] / [CO4]
  • Ans: The FEATURES table contains detailed biological annotations about the
  • sequence. (1 mark)
  • It includes the exact coordinates of genes, coding sequences (CDS), regulatory
  • regions, and the resulting protein translations. (1 mark)
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain the purpose of the Variant Effect Predictor (VEP) in Ensembl. / [CO4] [2x14 = 28]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the purpose of the Variant Effect Predictor (VEP) in Ensembl. [U] / [CO4]
  • Ans: VEP is a bioinformatics tool used to analyze and predict the functional consequences of
  • genetic variants (such as SNPs or indels). (1 mark)
  • It determines how a specific mutation will affect a transcript or protein (e.g., causing a frameshift
  • or missense mutation) and cross-references clinical databases to assess its potential to cause
  • disease. (1 mark)

questions.question: Explain the major components of media (salts, glucose, amino acids, vitamins, serum, antibiotics) and their roles. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the major components of media (salts, glucose, amino acids,
  • vitamins, serum, antibiotics) and their roles.
  • Ans: Basal Medium (Salts, Glucose, Amino Acids, Vitamins): Provide
  • essential nutrients, energy, and maintain osmotic pressure/pH for basic cell
  • survival. (1.5 marks)
  • Serum (e.g., FBS): Provides crucial growth factors, hormones, and attachment
  • factors required for active cell proliferation. (1.5 marks)
  • Antibiotics: Prevent bacterial and fungal contamination during culture
  • establishment. (1 mark)

questions.question: Explain the step-by-step procedure for starting a primary cell culture from a biological specimen. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the step-by-step procedure for starting a primary cell culture from a
  • biological specimen. [U] / [CO1]
  • Ans: Collection & Mincing: Harvesting tissue safely and mincing it into < 1 mm³
  • pieces. (1 mark)
  • Disaggregation: Using mechanical forces or enzymatic digestion
  • (Trypsin/Collagenase) to break the extracellular matrix and release single cells. (1.5
  • marks)
  • Filtering & Seeding: Filtering out large debris, washing the cells, and seeding them
  • into a culture vessel with appropriate media. (1.5 marks)

questions.question: Explain the function of Taq polymerase in PCR and its importance in the amplification process. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the function of Taq polymerase in PCR and its importance in
  • the amplification process.
  • Ans: Definition/Source: A thermostable DNA polymerase isolated from
  • Thermus aquaticus. (1 mark)
  • Importance in Denaturation: It can withstand the extreme heat (94–98°C)
  • required to separate DNA strands without denaturing itself. (1.5 marks)
  • Role in Extension: Synthesizes the new DNA strand at 72°C by adding dNTPs
  • in the 5' to 3' direction. (1.5 marks)
  • [U] / [CO2]

questions.question: Analyze the principles and applications of quantitative PCR (q PCR), explaining how it enables precise measurement of initial DNA or RNA quantities. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Analyse the principles and applications of quantitative PCR (qPCR),
  • explaining how it enables precise measurement of initial DNA or RNA
  • quantities. [An] / [CO2]
  • Ans: Principle: Uses fluorescent dyes (SYBR Green) or probes (TaqMan) to monitor
  • DNA amplification continuously in real-time. (2 marks)
  • Application: Enables precise measurement and absolute/relative quantification of
  • the initial amount of target DNA/RNA, unlike traditional end-point PCR. (2 marks)
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Describe the role of next-generation sequencing in diagnostic gene panels and evaluate its effectiveness. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Describe the role of next-generation sequencing in diagnostic gene panels
  • and evaluate its effectiveness.
  • Ans: Role: Allows simultaneous sequencing of a predefined group of genes
  • associated with specific diseases. (1 mark)
  • Advantages: High throughput, fast, cost-effective per base, and excellent for
  • hereditary disease screening. (1.5 marks)
  • Limitations: Strictly limited to the pre-selected genes; cannot detect mutations
  • in novel genes not included in the panel design. (1.5 marks)
  • [E] / [CO3]

questions.question: Evaluate whether Targeted Exome Sequencing is suitable for prenatal or pediatric genetic testing. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Evaluate whether Targeted Exome Sequencing is suitable for prenatal
  • or pediatric genetic testing.
  • Ans: Suitability: Highly suitable only if the target genes/phenotypes are
  • previously known. (1 mark)
  • Advantages: High coverage depth, reliability for low-frequency variants,
  • and faster/cheaper than Whole Genome Sequencing. (1.5 marks)
  • Limitations: Not suitable for diagnosing entirely new, complex, or
  • unknown genetic disorders where the causative gene is outside the targeted
  • exome. (1.5 marks)
  • [E] / [CO3]
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Evaluate the role of primer design in determining the success and specificity of Sanger sequencing. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Evaluate the role of primer design in determining the success and
  • specificity of Sanger sequencing. [E] / [CO3]
  • Ans: Primers dictate the exact starting point and specificity of the sequencing
  • reaction. Poor primers lead to unreadable chromatograms. (1.5 marks)
  • Design Parameters: Must have optimal length (18–25 bp), balanced GC content
  • (40-60%), and correctly calculated melting temperatures. (1.5 marks)
  • Must avoid secondary structures (hairpins) and primer-dimer formations. (1 mark)
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Discuss the scope and significance of Bioinformatics in modern genomic research. / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Discuss the scope and significance of Bioinformatics in modern genomic
  • research. [U] / [CO4]
  • Ans: Scope: Merges biology, computer science, and statistics for database
  • management, sequence analysis, and structural modelling. (1.5 marks)
  • Big Data Significance: Essential for storing, processing, and interpreting
  • the massive terabytes of raw data generated by NGS. (1 mark)
  • Applications: Powers variant prediction tools for diagnostics, and aids in
  • drug discovery and personalised medicine. (1.5 marks)
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Detail the utility of literature databases like Pub Med in genomics / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Detail the utility of literature databases like PubMed in genomics [U] / [CO4]
  • Ans: Repository: Acts as the central, searchable repository for peer-reviewed biomedical
  • literature. (1 mark)
  • Validation: Allows researchers to perform literature mining to check if newly discovered
  • variants have been clinically reported elsewhere. (1.5 marks)
  • Integration: Links raw sequence data (from databases like GenBank) directly to the published
  • biological research explaining its function. (1.5 marks)

questions.question: What is meant by "Genome Annotation"? Distinguish between structural and functional annotation / [CO4] [4x8 = 32]
questions.solution_html:
• What is meant by "Genome Annotation"? Distinguish between structural
  • and functional annotation. [U] / [CO4]
  • Ans: Definition: The process of identifying the locations of genes in a genome and
  • assigning biological meaning to them. (1 mark)
  • Structural Annotation: Locating the physical boundaries of genes—identifying
  • precise locations of exons, introns, and regulatory promoters. (1.5 marks)
  • Functional Annotation: Assigning biological roles to those genes, identifying
  • protein domains, and mapping them to metabolic pathways. (1.5 marks)
  • [4x8 = 32]
